sectionGuide.why: Many apparent reasoning errors are grounding failures — stale sources, wrong entities, ungrounded claims. This section names how outputs relate to authoritative world state: trust anchors, evidence, tool results, and external context.
sectionGuide.wgUse: World-ring vocabulary for gap analysis — separate model error from stale API or wrong entity. Hallucination subtypes in failure vocabulary refine these failures. Identity & Trust WG owns trust frameworks; ARWG owns measurement-facing definitions.
sectionGuide.enables: Hallucination subtypes refine grounding failures; evidence accuracy in core properties becomes operational; gap analysis can separate “model wrong” from “world or API wrong”.
sectionGuide.priorities: **P0** = grounding, trust anchor, evidence accuracy — minimum to classify a claim as grounded or not. **P1** = operational evidence types (tool result, provenance, ground truth). **P2** = evaluation infrastructure (knowledge base, annotations, session memory). Review P0 before hallucination subtypes.

categories.relevance: Evidence sources, memory, and retrieval artefacts that connect agent outputs to authoritative world state.
categories.wgUse: Benchmark harness rows · tool and orchestrator integration · inventory columns

categories.relevance: Evidence accuracy as a measurable output-quality property tied to grounding.
categories.wgUse: Enterprise checklists · judge rubrics where evidence must be verified

terms.definition: The degree to which claims, decisions, and recommended actions are tied to identifiable evidence, tool results, or authorised data sources rather than model parametric guesswork alone.
terms.scopeNote: Central to evidence accuracy and hallucination subtyping. Trust requirements and anchors defined further in trust frameworks.
terms.literatureNote: Generally accepted in RAG evaluation; AAIF extends to tool results and trust anchors, not only retrieved passages.

terms.definition: An authoritative data source, service, or verification rule against which an agent output can be checked for high-stakes tasks.
terms.scopeNote: Charter assumption for enterprise verification. Detailed protocols are a Phase 3 deliverable.
terms.literatureNote: Harness and participant vocabulary for gap analysis inventory. Describes how measurement runs, not agent properties.

terms.definition: Whether the facts, citations, and observations cited in support of a conclusion are complete, relevant, and faithful to available sources.
terms.scopeNote: Supports audit and grounding checks. High evidence accuracy does not guarantee the final decision is right.
terms.literatureNote: Task-result vocabulary bridging accuracy to user-visible outcomes. Common in benchmark reporting with varying definitions.
